title: Tanzanian Goat Stew
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Mchuzi wa Mbuzi — Tanzanian goat stew. Young goat simmered slowly in a rich tomato-onion sauce fragrant with cumin, coriander, and garlic until the meat is falling off the bone. The stew served at every Tanzanian celebration and every important family gathering.
longDesc: Goat is the most celebratory meat in Tanzania — when a goat is slaughtered, it signals a significant occasion. Mchuzi wa Mbuzi is the slow-cooked stew made from that goat — patient, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. The collagen from goat bones creates a silky sauce that coats ugali perfectly.
steps: Brown goat pieces in hot oil. Remove.
Add garlic, ginger, and spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook until completely reduced — 10 minutes.
Simmer covered on very low heat for 75—90 minutes until meat falls from bone.
chefTips: Young goat (mbuzi mdogo) is most tender.
Very low heat for the simmer — goat toughens if boiled hard.
The longer the simmer, the better.
commonMistakes: Young goat is essential — old goat requires 3+ hours.
cookingScience: Goat contains more collagen than beef at the same cut — particularly around the joints and bone. Extended slow cooking converts this to gelatin, producing an exceptionally rich, silky sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Goat is the most sustainable red meat — lower water and land footprint than beef.
healthBenefits: Goat is leaner than beef or lamb.
culturalNote: Goat stew is Tanzania's most celebratory everyday meat dish — eaten at naming ceremonies, circumcisions, homecomings, and harvests. The slaughter of a goat for a guest is among the highest expressions of Tanzanian hospitality.
